title: How does the Next.js shell import lib/ without duplicating it?
statement: The shell must consume the existing lint, derivation, locking and typed-operation modules as the single implementation (#47), rather than reimplementing any of them inside the application. The mechanism — path resolution, bundling behaviour, and which modules may run in a browser context at all — is unsettled.
notes: ⚠️ The constraint is #47's own: one implementation, several callers. The app is the second caller the lint was designed for. The real difficulty is that these modules are Node-only — they read the filesystem, take locks and spawn processes — so the boundary between what runs on the server and what reaches the client is the actual subject of this question, not the import syntax. ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-08-26 (AST-0032, AST-0033; EVD-0045..EVD-0048 sourced, EVD-0049 and EVD-0050 experimental). PROPOSAL MADE, NOT DECIDED — stage 5 is agent-proposes-user-approves (#34). ⚠️ THE IMPORT MECHANISM IS A NON-PROBLEM, which is worth saying plainly because the question assumed otherwise: a Server Component imports a sibling `lib/` module by plain relative path and it builds and runs. No alias, no `transpilePackages`, no bundler configuration. #47's single implementation needs nothing special to stay single. ⚠️ THE REAL SUBJECT IS THE BOUNDARY, as the question's own note predicted, and the documented hazard is transitive: a `'use client'` file drags ALL of its imports into the client bundle (EVD-0046). Both client-import cases already fail the build — so the risk is not that Node-only code ships to a browser, it is that the failure is UNREADABLE. Unguarded, Turbopack reports an internal error with `location: undefined` and no filename. ⚠️ PROPOSAL: a thin `app/server/*` adapter layer carrying `import 'server-only'` and re-exporting from `lib/`, with application code importing the adapter and never `lib/` directly. Measured to work in both directions, and it is forced rather than chosen — the guard CANNOT go in `lib/`, because `server-only` throws under plain Node and `lib/` is imported by every `bin/` command and the whole test suite. ⚠️ IT WANTS REQ-0021'S CHECK, NOT A SECOND ONE. The adapter is a convention until something enforces it; a component can import `../../lib/x.mjs` and bypass the guard. That is the same static-confinement rule REQ-0021 already requires for planning-content reads, with a second forbidden edge rather than a new mechanism. ⚠️ NOT MEASURED: whether every module the shell needs can be re-exported this way — some take locks, spawn processes, or hold module-level state — and whether the unguarded failure differs under webpack. ⚠️ NOTHING HERE TOUCHES CACHE COMPONENTS.
